Prevention: February in medium and high altitudes to avoid major bug occurrence.
Sow during the first planting rains for
Plant with spacing of 20 cm by 75 cm apart.
Mix the crop stand soon after planting when the cowpea has germinated, for example with repellent plants like garlic or
Ha to make cowpea more tolerant to insects and to increase yield.
Remove and compost residues from previous crop as insects may over-season in debris.
However, if no major diseases or pests are in your field, keep residues to improve soil and preserve water.
Monitoring: Scout for insects and damage from flower- budding to pod formation stage, this is 30 to 35 days after planting, every week or second week.
Look for brown bugs, 15 to 16 mm long with flat legs.
They have a triangle plate behind the head.
Find them on pods or under leaves in the morning when active.
Look for shrivelled and premature dried pods, note that these symptoms can be mistaken by water stress, feeding puncture wounds are a symptom of pod-sucking bugs.
Consider taking action when a threshold of 2 to 3 bugs per 10 plants is reached, or 2-3 bugs/ metre row.
Direct Control: Preventive cultural control alone is often not enough to control pod-sucking bugs.
Regularly collect and destroy bugs by hand in small plots during flowering and pod formation.
But do not collect natural enemies you observe in the field such as assassin bugs, spiders, praying mantises and ants.
Spray neem seed solutions (210 g/ acre) crushed and soaked in water over night, spray when needed 3 times at 7 days intervals starting from pod formation.
Malathion –based products (organophosphate), 14 to 25ml in 10L of water
Cypermethrin – based products (pyrethroid), 2.5 to 5ml in 20L of water
Restrictions: Max 2 sprays per season if thresholds are reached at the beginning of pod formation at a minimum interval of 10 days; in the morning hours but when there is no dew or in late evening.
Alternate pesticides to reduce developing pest resistances.
Wear protective clothing when using a pesticide or botanical.
Always follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not eat, drink and smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
